title: tsbench: a benchmark of language models on Tanabe-Sugano ligand-field tasks
description:
The TS-MCP benchmark (tsbench): language models fit the ligand-field parameters Dq, B and C to absorption spectra, compute Tanabe-Sugano curves and term diagrams, find spin crossovers and recognise questions outside the ligand-field model. Each task runs under three tool conditions: no tools (A), a code interpreter in a sandbox with a fixed Python stack (B), and the TanabeSugano MCP server (C).

The data set contains the generated task set of 105 tasks (50 pilot, 55 confirmatory) with its oracles, tolerances and hashes, the prompts and answer schemas, the run planner and the runner with its sandbox and its fake claude for dry runs, the scorer, the statistics, and the code that draws the figures and renders the report pages, with its tests. The confirmatory study follows the preregistered protocol and sealed run plans of the related record; the task set hashes and the git tree hash named there identify the code the runs were made with (commit e7f9560, the first commit of this repository). The second commit adds the analysis, report and CI code and the data.

The folder results/ holds the data of the confirmatory study: the four preregistered run plans (plan 1: claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-opus-5-5; plans 2a to 2c: gemma-4-31b-it, qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507 and qwen3.5-397b-a17b), 2970 evaluated runs with every transcript, sidecar, retried attempt and manifest, the scores, the tests of the primary and the secondary family, the images and code the models produced, offline analyses, and the reports. Machine paths and names are replaced by placeholders, and REDACTIONS.csv and SHA256SUMS record every changed and every published file.
